opinions.rationale: Treatment-version ambiguity is real: collapsing causally different doses, formulations, routes, combinations, or adherence patterns can make the named intervention ill-defined. However, the report overstates both the required mechanics and the remaining gap. Estimating a per-protocol effect does not require artificial censoring plus inverse-probability weighting; the longitudinal g-formula and targeted or sequential-regression estimators can estimate sustained-strategy effects under their respective identification and modeling conditions. Clone-censor-weight already provides the bookkeeping for individuals compatible with multiple prespecified strategies, although it cannot choose those strategies or determine which versions are equivalent. Observed data cannot prove treatment-version irrelevance, but version-specific data can reveal heterogeneity and inform clinical judgment. Finer definitions may worsen practical support and precision, but every additional strategy does not mechanically violate positivity. Pinned lmtp 1.5.4 is correctly described: its NAMESPACE exports lmtp_tmle and lmtp_sdr, while its source accepts list-valued treatment nodes and applies analyst-specified multivariate shifts. It therefore supports estimation after a joint policy has been defined, not construction of clinical equivalence classes. Moreover, a longitudinal modified treatment policy generally targets a natural-value-dependent policy estimand, not automatically the per-protocol effect of a fixed sustained strategy. The issue is decision-critical when collapsed versions have materially different effects; a universal treatment ontology or latent-version model is a roadmap item rather than a prerequisite for every well-specified emulation.
opinions.weakest_true_restatement: Analysts must clinically specify sustained strategies and relevant treatment versions before estimating a per-protocol effect. Artificial censoring and inverse-probability weighting are one valid estimation approach, not a universal requirement. Clone-censor-weight handles individuals compatible with multiple predefined strategies but does not determine whether treatment versions should be pooled. Observed data alone cannot establish treatment-version irrelevance, although they can expose heterogeneity, and finer definitions may create practical support problems. Longitudinal multivariate modified-treatment-policy estimators can estimate an analyst-specified joint policy but do not supply the clinical equivalence classes or necessarily target the same per-protocol estimand.

resolving_work.title: De-Mystifying the Clone-Censor-Weight Method for Causal Research Using Observational Data: A Primer for Cancer Researchers
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Provides the cloning, artificial-censoring, and weighting procedure for individuals whose observed histories are simultaneously compatible with multiple predefined strategies. It does not determine which treatment versions should constitute a strategy.

resolving_work.title: lmtp: Non-Parametric Causal Effects of Feasible Interventions Based on Modified Treatment Policies
resolving_work.what_it_resolves: Pinned source exports longitudinal TMLE and sequentially doubly robust estimators and implements analyst-specified multivariate treatment shifts. This resolves the joint-policy estimation component after treatment variables and the intervention have been defined, but not equivalence-class construction.
